Behavioral Health Response Team (BHRT): BHRT is dispatched through the 911 system and has the ability to provide either a co-response—pairing behavioral health crisis counselors with specially trained officers —or a Clinician Alternative Response (CAR), where two Community Safety Department staff respond to appropriate, low-risk calls in lieu of law enforcement.
Note: Response area may not include entire county. Depending on the call type and team availability, police / fire / EMS may be sent instead.

The BEAR Team responds 24/7 to mental health and substance use emergencies in Winston-Salem.
Fast response - usually within 30 minutes.
Works with local partners for follow-up care.

Description:
Asheville Fire Department (AFD) Community Responders will be the lead and first on-the-scene operational response agency to support people in crisis and mitigate the communitywide effects of homelessness. Community Responders are actively reimagining public safety by helping to make connections to resources and providing services when no law is being broken.
Team covers all areas within Asheville City limits and serves as the primary response to encampments
